tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.

Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). """The worker's loop: claim queued runs one at a time, run them, and stop cleanly.

Kept apart from main.py (which initialises neatlogs on import) so it can be tested. It also
holds what a server needs:

  * a health line once a minute while idle, so `docker logs` shows the worker is alive and waiting;
  * a heartbeat file, touched while the process is alive, which the Docker HEALTHCHECK reads;
  * graceful shutdown on SIGTERM (what `docker stop` sends) and SIGINT: the run in progress is
    finished and saved first, then the process exits. A second signal stops immediately; the run is
    left "running" and a later stale-run sweep marks it failed.
"""

import asyncio
import signal
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

IDLE_SECONDS = 2
STALE_MINUTES = 15
STALE_SWEEP_SECONDS = 60
# A test login still in the database this long after it was queued is deleted unread.
SECRETS_MINUTES = 30
DB_ERROR_BACKOFF_SECONDS = 10
HEARTBEAT_SECONDS = 5


def _duration(seconds: float) -> str:
    seconds = int(seconds)
    hours, rest = divmod(seconds, 3600)
    minutes, secs = divmod(rest, 60)
    if hours:
        return f"{hours}h{minutes:02d}m"
    return f"{minutes}m{secs:02d}s" if minutes else f"{secs}s"


class Worker:
    def __init__(self, agent_version: str, *, db, execute, brain_model: str, health_interval: float = 60,
                 health_file: str | None = None, idle_seconds: float = IDLE_SECONDS,
                 heartbeat_seconds: float = HEARTBEAT_SECONDS, clock=time.monotonic):
        self.agent_version, self.db, self.execute, self.brain_model = agent_version, db, execute, brain_model
        self.health_interval, self.health_file = health_interval, health_file
        self.idle_seconds, self.heartbeat_seconds, self.clock = idle_seconds, heartbeat_seconds, clock
        self.stop_requested = False
        self.state = "starting"  # starting | idle | running | stopping
        self.started_at = self.idle_since = clock()
        self.runs_done = self.runs_failed = self.db_errors = 0

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- stopping
    def request_stop(self, why: str = "stop requested") -> None:
        if not self.stop_requested:
            self.stop_requested = True
            print(f"{why}: finishing the current run (if any), then exiting.", flush=True)

    def on_signal(self, signum, frame) -> None:
        """First signal: stop after the current run. Second: stop now."""
        if self.stop_requested:
            raise KeyboardInterrupt
        name = signal.Signals(signum).name if signum in signal.Signals._value2member_map_ else str(signum)
        self.request_stop(f"Received {name}")

    def install_signal_handlers(self) -> None:
        for name in ("SIGINT", "SIGTERM", "SIGBREAK"):  # SIGBREAK is Windows' Ctrl+Break
            if hasattr(signal, name):
                signal.signal(getattr(signal, name), self.on_signal)

    async def _sleep_unless_stopping(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        deadline = self.clock() + seconds
        while not self.stop_requested and self.clock() < deadline:
            await asyncio.sleep(min(0.2, max(0.0, deadline - self.clock())))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- health
    def health_line(self) -> str:
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        parts = [f"[health] {now}", self.state]
        if self.state == "idle":
            parts.append(f"for {_duration(self.clock() - self.idle_since)}, queue empty")
        parts.append(f"| {self.runs_done} runs since start ({self.runs_failed} failed)")
        parts.append(f"| up {_duration(self.clock() - self.started_at)}")
        parts.append(f"| agent {self.agent_version}")
        if self.db_errors:
            parts.append(f"| {self.db_errors} database errors in a row")
        return " ".join(parts)

    async def _heartbeat(self) -> None:
        """Touch the heartbeat file, and log a health line every health_interval while idle."""
        last_line = self.clock()
        while True:
            if self.health_file:
                try:
                    Path(self.health_file).touch()
                except OSError:
                    pass
            # Half a tick of tolerance, so a 60 s interval is 60 s and not 65.
            if self.state == "idle" and self.clock() - last_line >= self.health_interval - self.heartbeat_seconds / 2:
                print(self.health_line(), flush=True)
                last_line = self.clock()
            elif self.state != "idle":
                last_line = self.clock()
            await asyncio.sleep(self.heartbeat_seconds)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- the loop
    async def run(self) -> None:
        print(f"Worker started (agent {self.agent_version}, brain {self.brain_model}). "
              "Waiting for queued runs.", flush=True)
        heartbeat = asyncio.create_task(self._heartbeat())
        last_sweep = float("-inf")
        self.state = "idle"
        self.idle_since = self.clock()
        try:
            while not self.stop_requested:
                try:
                    if self.clock() - last_sweep >= STALE_SWEEP_SECONDS:
                        last_sweep = self.clock()
                        for stale in await self.db.fail_stale_runs(STALE_MINUTES):
                            print(f"Marked stale run {stale['id']} as failed", flush=True)
                        await self.db.delete_old_run_secrets(SECRETS_MINUTES)
                    run = await self.db.claim_run()
                    self.db_errors = 0
                except Exception as error:
                    self.db_errors += 1
                    print(f"Database error: {type(error).__name__}: {error}; "
                          f"retrying in {DB_ERROR_BACKOFF_SECONDS}s", flush=True)
                    await self._sleep_unless_stopping(DB_ERROR_BACKOFF_SECONDS)
                    continue

                if run is None:
                    if self.state != "idle":
                        self.state, self.idle_since = "idle", self.clock()
                    await self._sleep_unless_stopping(self.idle_seconds)
                    continue
                self.state = "running"
                try:
                    await self.execute(run, self.agent_version)
                    self.runs_done += 1
                except Exception as error:
                    # Saving the outcome failed; the stale-run sweep will mark the run failed later.
                    self.runs_failed += 1
                    print(f"Could not save run {run['id']}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}", flush=True)
                self.state, self.idle_since = "idle", self.clock()

            self.state = "stopping"
            heartbeat.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(heartbeat, return_exceptions=True)
"""Execute one claimed run: load its test login, run the visit, save the outcome, clear the login.

Kept apart from main.py (which initialises neatlogs and owns the signal handlers when it is
imported) so that the whole path can be tested with a stand-in database.
"""

import shutil
import traceback

import neatlogs

import db
import trace_safety
from config import BRAIN_MODEL, CLEAN_RUN_FILES
from credentials import TestCredentials
from tools import RUNS_DIR
from visit import first_visit


def _clean_run_files(run_id: str) -> None:
    """Delete the run's local screenshots (CLEAN_RUN_FILES): they were uploaded, and a server's disk
    would otherwise fill up. Left alone by default, for debugging on a laptop."""
    if CLEAN_RUN_FILES:
        shutil.rmtree(RUNS_DIR / run_id, ignore_errors=True)


ACCESS_MODES = ("public", "link", "account", "signup")


def access_mode_for(run: dict) -> str:
    """How the founder let the visitor in.

    Runs from the web form carry it. Runs queued before that (and from the command line) are read
    from what they have: a test login, a start link, or neither, which meant "may sign up".
    """
    mode = run.get("access_mode")
    if mode in ACCESS_MODES:
        return mode
    if run.get("has_test_login"):
        return "account"
    if run.get("start_url"):
        return "link"
    return "signup"


def access_mode_was_chosen(run: dict) -> bool:
    """False only when "signup" is the fallback for a run that carried no choice and nothing to infer one from."""
    return run.get("access_mode") in ACCESS_MODES or bool(run.get("has_test_login") or run.get("start_url"))


async def _take_credentials(run: dict):
    """The run's test login, read and deleted from the database, or (None, unavailable)."""
    if not run.get("has_test_login"):
        return None, False
    try:
        row = await db.take_run_secrets(run["id"])
    except Exception as error:
        # The type only: the message is not needed, and nothing about a login should be logged.
        print(f"Could not read the test login for run {run['id']}: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return None, True
    if row is None:
        return None, True
    credentials = TestCredentials(row["email"], row["password"])
    credentials.register()  # redacted from every span and result from this moment on
    return credentials, False


async def execute(run: dict, agent_version: str) -> None:
    run_id = run["id"]
    start_url = run.get("start_url")
    access_mode = access_mode_for(run)
    print(f"Claimed run {run_id}: {run['url']}" + (f" (start link {start_url})" if start_url else "")
          + f" (access {access_mode}, brain {BRAIN_MODEL}, agent {agent_version})", flush=True)
    credentials, unavailable = await _take_credentials(run)
    try:
        with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"run_{run_id}"):
            result = await first_visit(
                run["url"], run["goal"], run_id, recorder=db.RunRecorder(run_id),
                start_url=start_url, credentials=credentials, test_login_unavailable=unavailable,
                access_mode=access_mode, access_mode_chosen=access_mode_was_chosen(run),
            )
    except Exception as error:
        # Error text and tracebacks pass through scrub(): an exception can echo what was typed.
        message = trace_safety.scrub(f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        print(trace_safety.scrub(traceback.format_exc()), flush=True)
        await db.fail_run(run_id, message, agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL)
        print(f"Run {run_id} failed: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return
    finally:
        # take_run_secrets already deleted it; this is the safety net, success or failure.
        await db.delete_run_secrets(run_id)
        _clean_run_files(run_id)

    if result["outcome"] == "error":
        await db.fail_run(run_id, result["reason"], agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL, result=result)
        print(f"Run {run_id} failed: {result['reason'][:200]}", flush=True)
    else:
        await db.finish_run(run_id, result, agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL)
        print(f"Run {run_id} done: {result['outcome']} in {result['steps']} steps", flush=True)

    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

    row = {"url": url, "goal": goal, "source": source}

        row["start_url"] = start_url
    response = await (await client()).table("runs").insert(row).execute()
    return response.data[0]


async def claim_run() -> dict | None:
    """Take the oldest queued run and mark it running, or return None if the queue is empty."""
    response = await (await client()).rpc("claim_run").execute()
    return response.data[0] if response.data else None


async def add_step(
    run_id: str,
    idx: int,
    tool: str,
    thought: str,
    input: dict,
    result: dict,
    url: str | None,
    screenshot_path: str | None = None,
) -> None:

        "run_id": run_id,
        "idx": idx,
        "tool": tool,

        "severity": severity,
        "expected": expected,
        "happened": happened,
    }).execute()


async def finish_run(run_id: str, result: dict, agent_version: str, brain_model: str) -> None:
    await _update_run(run_id, {
        "status": "done",
        "outcome": result.get("outcome"),
        "reason": result.get("reason"),
        "result": result,
        "cost_usd": result.get("usage", {}).get("estimated_cost_usd", {}).get("total"),
        "agent_version": agent_version,
        "brain_model": brain_model,
        "trace_id": result.get("trace_id"),
        "first_impression": result.get("first_impression"),
        "entry": result.get("entry"),
        "findings": result.get("findings"),
        "finished_at": _now(),
    })


# Columns added after the first schema. If the database does not have one yet (supabase/schema.sql
# not re-run), runs are saved without it and a warning is printed once, rather than failing.
OPTIONAL_COLUMNS = ("trace_id", "first_impression", "entry", "findings")
_missing_columns: set[str] = set()


async def _update_run(run_id: str, update: dict) -> None:
    update = {k: v for k, v in update.items() if k not in _missing_columns}
    try:
        await (await client()).table("runs").update(update).eq("id", run_id).execute()
    except Exception as error:
        missing = {c for c in OPTIONAL_COLUMNS if c in update and c in str(error)}
        if not missing:
            raise
        _missing_columns.update(missing)
        print(f"runs.{', runs.'.join(sorted(missing))} does not exist yet (run the last lines of "
              "supabase/schema.sql); saving runs without it.", flush=True)
        update = {k: v for k, v in update.items() if k not in _missing_columns}
        await (await client()).table("runs").update(update).eq("id", run_id).execute()


async def take_run_secrets(run_id: str) -> dict | None:
    """Read a run's test login and delete it from the database in the same statement.

    Returns {"email", "password"} or None if the run has none. After this call the database no
    longer holds the login; it lives only in the worker's memory for the run.
    """
    response = await (await client()).rpc("take_run_secrets", {"p_run_id": run_id}).execute()
    row = response.data[0] if response.data else None
    return {"email": row["test_email"], "password": row["test_password"]} if row else None


async def delete_run_secrets(run_id: str) -> None:
    """Safety net at the end of a run, whatever happened: no test login stays behind."""
    try:
        await (await client()).table("run_secrets").delete().eq("run_id", run_id).execute()
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"Could not clear the test login for run {run_id}: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)


async def delete_old_run_secrets(minutes: int = 30) -> None:
    """A test login whose run was never claimed (or never finished) is not kept."""
    cutoff = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=minutes)).isoformat()
    try:
        await (await client()).table("run_secrets").delete().lt("created_at", cutoff).execute()
    except Exception:
        pass


async def fail_run(
    run_id: str,
    error: str,
    agent_version: str | None = None,
    brain_model: str | None = None,
    result: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    update = {"status": "failed", "error": error[:2000], "finished_at": _now()}
    if agent_version:
        update["agent_version"] = agent_version
    if brain_model:
        update["brain_model"] = brain_model
    if result is not None:
        update.update({
            "outcome": result.get("outcome"),
            "reason": result.get("reason"),
            "result": result,
            "cost_usd": result.get("usage", {}).get("estimated_cost_usd", {}).get("total"),
            "trace_id": result.get("trace_id"),
            "first_impression": result.get("first_impression"),
            "entry": result.get("entry"),
            "findings": result.get("findings"),
        })
    await _update_run(run_id, update)


async def fail_stale_runs(minutes: int = 15) -> list[dict]:
    """Mark runs that have been running for longer than `minutes` as failed."""
    cutoff = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=minutes)).isoformat()
    response = await (await client()).table("runs").update({
        "status": "failed",
        "error": f"Stale: still running after {minutes} minutes (worker stopped or crashed).",
        "finished_at": _now(),
    }).eq("status", "running").lt("started_at", cutoff).execute()
    return response.data


async def upload_screenshot(run_id: str, local_path: Path) -> str:
    """Upload a PNG or JPEG to the public screenshots bucket and return its public URL."""
    storage_path = f"{run_id}/{local_path.name}"
    bucket = (await client()).storage.from_(BUCKET)
    content_type = "image/jpeg" if local_path.suffix.lower() in (".jpg", ".jpeg") else "image/png"
    await bucket.upload(
        storage_path,
        local_path.read_bytes(),
        {"content-type": content_type, "x-upsert": "true"},
    )
    return await bucket.get_public_url(storage_path)


class RunRecorder:
    """Writes one run's steps, frictions and screenshots to Supabase as they happen."""

    def __init__(self, run_id: str):
        self.run_id = run_id

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"RunRecorder(run_id={self.run_id!r})"

        """Upload one step's screenshot; do() calls this so the URL can go into its span output."""
        return await upload_screenshot(self.run_id, path)

        await add_step(self.run_id, idx, tool, thought, input, result, url, screenshot_url)

    async def friction(self, step_idx, kind, severity, expected, happened) -> None:
        await add_friction(self.run_id, step_idx, kind, severity, expected, happened)
"""Egress guard: a local proxy that every browser request must go through.

Chrome is launched with this proxy and with its implicit localhost bypass turned
off, so every navigation, redirect, subresource and websocket reaches it first.
For each new host the guard resolves the name itself, refuses it if any address
is private, loopback, link-local, cloud metadata or otherwise not public, and
then connects only to an address it vetted. Connecting to the vetted address
(not re-resolving) is what stops DNS rebinding.

A refusal is recorded on the guard; the agent loop ends the run as blocked.
"""

import asyncio
import contextvars
import ipaddress
import socket
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import neatlogs

CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15
HEADER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30
MAX_HEADER_BYTES = 64 * 1024
PIPE_CHUNK = 64 * 1024
NAT64 = ipaddress.ip_network("64:ff9b::/96")

# Chrome flags that go with the proxy: "<-loopback>" removes Chrome's built-in
# rule that sends localhost and 127.0.0.1 around the proxy, and WebRTC may not
# open UDP connections that would skip it.
CHROME_PROXY_BYPASS = "<-loopback>"
CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS = ["--force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp"]


def is_blocked_address(address: ipaddress.IPv4Address | ipaddress.IPv6Address) -> bool:
    """True for anything a public visitor's browser should never reach."""
    if isinstance(address, ipaddress.IPv6Address):
        if address.ipv4_mapped is not None:
            return is_blocked_address(address.ipv4_mapped)
        if address in NAT64:
            return is_blocked_address(ipaddress.IPv4Address(int(address) & 0xFFFFFFFF))
    # is_global is False for private, loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254, the
    # cloud metadata address), carrier-grade NAT, unique-local, documentation
    # and reserved ranges.
    return not address.is_global or address.is_multicast


@dataclass
class Decision:
    allowed: bool
    addresses: list[str]
    reason: str = ""
    private: bool = False  # refused for safety, as opposed to simply not resolving


@dataclass
class EgressGuard:
    blocks: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    _decisions: dict[str, Decision] = field(default_factory=dict)
    _locks: dict[str, asyncio.Lock] = field(default_factory=dict)
    _server: asyncio.AbstractServer | None = None
    _context: contextvars.Context | None = None
    # True while the guard belongs to an active neatlogs run (see start()).
    _traced: bool = False
    # One task per open browser connection, so close() can cancel the ones still piping.
    _connections: set[asyncio.Task] = field(default_factory=set)
    port: int = 0
    # Chrome's own DevTools port. Stagehand's extension, running inside Chrome,
    # connects to it, so that one tunnel is allowed, but only for an extension.
    devtools_port: int | None = None

        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}"

    async def start(self) -> None:

        # no neatlogs run active (tests, scripts), the guard creates no spans at all.
        self._context = contextvars.copy_context()
        self._traced = neatlogs.inject_trace_context({})
        self._server = await asyncio.start_server(self._handle, "127.0.0.1", 0)
        self.port = self._server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Stop accepting connections, then cancel and await the ones still open.

        Cancelled connections create no spans: host checks are not traced, and a refusal
        span is created and ended in one synchronous call.
        """
        if self._server is None:
            return
        self._traced = False
        self._server.close()
        connections = list(self._connections)
        for task in connections:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*connections, return_exceptions=True)
        await self._server.wait_closed()
        self._server = None

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        """Hosts checked and refused during the run, for one summary on the run's trace."""
        refused = sorted({block["host"] for block in self.blocks})
        return {
            "hosts_checked": len(self._decisions),
            "hosts_allowed": sum(d.allowed for d in self._decisions.values()),
            "hosts_unresolved": sum(not d.allowed and not d.private for d in self._decisions.values()),
            "hosts_refused": refused,
            "refusals": len(self.blocks),

    def _refused(self, record: dict) -> None:
        """Record a refusal, with a GUARDRAIL span in the run's trace while the run is active."""
        self.blocks.append(record)

            self._context.copy().run(_refusal_span, record)

    def block_reason(self) -> str | None:

        if not self.blocks:

        return (
            f"Stopped for safety: the site sent the browser to {first['host']}, which is a private, local or "
            f"cloud-metadata address ({', '.join(first['addresses'])}). "
            "First User never visits those, so the visit ended here."

Chrome is launched with this proxy and with its implicit localhost bypass turned

then connects only to an address it vetted. Connecting to the vetted address
(not re-resolving) is what stops DNS rebinding.

def is_blocked_address(address: ipaddress.IPv4Address | ipaddress.IPv6Address) -> bool:
    """True for anything a public visitor's browser should never reach."""
    if isinstance(address, ipaddress.IPv6Address):

        if address in NAT64:

    # cloud metadata address), carrier-grade NAT, unique-local, documentation
    # and reserved ranges.
    return not address.is_global or address.is_multicast

(not re-resolving) is what stops DNS rebinding.

def is_blocked_address(address: ipaddress.IPv4Address | ipaddress.IPv6Address) -> bool:
    """True for anything a public visitor's browser should never reach."""
    if isinstance(address, ipaddress.IPv6Address):
        if address.ipv4_mapped is not None:

    # cloud metadata address), carrier-grade NAT, unique-local, documentation
    # and reserved ranges.
    return not address.is_global or address.is_multicast

"""The worker's loop: claim queued runs one at a time, run them, and stop cleanly.

Kept apart from main.py (which initialises neatlogs on import) so it can be tested. It also
holds what a server needs:

  * a health line once a minute while idle, so `docker logs` shows the worker is alive and waiting;
  * a heartbeat file, touched while the process is alive, which the Docker HEALTHCHECK reads;
  * graceful shutdown on SIGTERM (what `docker stop` sends) and SIGINT: the run in progress is
    finished and saved first, then the process exits. A second signal stops immediately; the run is
    left "running" and a later stale-run sweep marks it failed.
"""

import asyncio
import signal
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

IDLE_SECONDS = 2
STALE_MINUTES = 15
STALE_SWEEP_SECONDS = 60
# A test login still in the database this long after it was queued is deleted unread.
SECRETS_MINUTES = 30
DB_ERROR_BACKOFF_SECONDS = 10
HEARTBEAT_SECONDS = 5


def _duration(seconds: float) -> str:
    seconds = int(seconds)
    hours, rest = divmod(seconds, 3600)
    minutes, secs = divmod(rest, 60)
    if hours:
        return f"{hours}h{minutes:02d}m"
    return f"{minutes}m{secs:02d}s" if minutes else f"{secs}s"


class Worker:
    def __init__(self, agent_version: str, *, db, execute, brain_model: str, health_interval: float = 60,
                 health_file: str | None = None, idle_seconds: float = IDLE_SECONDS,
                 heartbeat_seconds: float = HEARTBEAT_SECONDS, clock=time.monotonic):
        self.agent_version, self.db, self.execute, self.brain_model = agent_version, db, execute, brain_model
        self.health_interval, self.health_file = health_interval, health_file
        self.idle_seconds, self.heartbeat_seconds, self.clock = idle_seconds, heartbeat_seconds, clock
        self.stop_requested = False
        self.state = "starting"  # starting | idle | running | stopping
        self.started_at = self.idle_since = clock()
        self.runs_done = self.runs_failed = self.db_errors = 0

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- stopping
    def request_stop(self, why: str = "stop requested") -> None:
        if not self.stop_requested:
            self.stop_requested = True
            print(f"{why}: finishing the current run (if any), then exiting.", flush=True)

    def on_signal(self, signum, frame) -> None:
        """First signal: stop after the current run. Second: stop now."""
        if self.stop_requested:
            raise KeyboardInterrupt
        name = signal.Signals(signum).name if signum in signal.Signals._value2member_map_ else str(signum)
        self.request_stop(f"Received {name}")

    def install_signal_handlers(self) -> None:
        for name in ("SIGINT", "SIGTERM", "SIGBREAK"):  # SIGBREAK is Windows' Ctrl+Break
            if hasattr(signal, name):
                signal.signal(getattr(signal, name), self.on_signal)

    async def _sleep_unless_stopping(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        deadline = self.clock() + seconds
        while not self.stop_requested and self.clock() < deadline:
            await asyncio.sleep(min(0.2, max(0.0, deadline - self.clock())))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- health
    def health_line(self) -> str:
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        parts = [f"[health] {now}", self.state]
        if self.state == "idle":
            parts.append(f"for {_duration(self.clock() - self.idle_since)}, queue empty")
        parts.append(f"| {self.runs_done} runs since start ({self.runs_failed} failed)")
        parts.append(f"| up {_duration(self.clock() - self.started_at)}")
        parts.append(f"| agent {self.agent_version}")
        if self.db_errors:
            parts.append(f"| {self.db_errors} database errors in a row")
        return " ".join(parts)

    async def _heartbeat(self) -> None:
        """Touch the heartbeat file, and log a health line every health_interval while idle."""
        last_line = self.clock()
        while True:
            if self.health_file:
                try:
                    Path(self.health_file).touch()
                except OSError:
                    pass
            # Half a tick of tolerance, so a 60 s interval is 60 s and not 65.
            if self.state == "idle" and self.clock() - last_line >= self.health_interval - self.heartbeat_seconds / 2:
                print(self.health_line(), flush=True)
                last_line = self.clock()
            elif self.state != "idle":
                last_line = self.clock()
            await asyncio.sleep(self.heartbeat_seconds)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- the loop
    async def run(self) -> None:
        print(f"Worker started (agent {self.agent_version}, brain {self.brain_model}). "
              "Waiting for queued runs.", flush=True)
        heartbeat = asyncio.create_task(self._heartbeat())
        last_sweep = float("-inf")
        self.state = "idle"
        self.idle_since = self.clock()
        try:
            while not self.stop_requested:
                try:
                    if self.clock() - last_sweep >= STALE_SWEEP_SECONDS:
                        last_sweep = self.clock()
                        for stale in await self.db.fail_stale_runs(STALE_MINUTES):
                            print(f"Marked stale run {stale['id']} as failed", flush=True)
                        await self.db.delete_old_run_secrets(SECRETS_MINUTES)
                    run = await self.db.claim_run()
                    self.db_errors = 0
                except Exception as error:
                    self.db_errors += 1
                    print(f"Database error: {type(error).__name__}: {error}; "
                          f"retrying in {DB_ERROR_BACKOFF_SECONDS}s", flush=True)
                    await self._sleep_unless_stopping(DB_ERROR_BACKOFF_SECONDS)
                    continue

                if run is None:
                    if self.state != "idle":
                        self.state, self.idle_since = "idle", self.clock()
                    await self._sleep_unless_stopping(self.idle_seconds)
                    continue
                self.state = "running"
                try:
                    await self.execute(run, self.agent_version)
                    self.runs_done += 1
                except Exception as error:
                    # Saving the outcome failed; the stale-run sweep will mark the run failed later.
                    self.runs_failed += 1
                    print(f"Could not save run {run['id']}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}", flush=True)
                self.state, self.idle_since = "idle", self.clock()
        finally:
            self.state = "stopping"
            heartbeat.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(heartbeat, return_exceptions=True)
"""Execute one claimed run: load its test login, run the visit, save the outcome, clear the login.

Kept apart from main.py (which initialises neatlogs and owns the signal handlers when it is
imported) so that the whole path can be tested with a stand-in database.
"""

import shutil
import traceback

import neatlogs

import db
import trace_safety
from config import BRAIN_MODEL, CLEAN_RUN_FILES
from credentials import TestCredentials
from tools import RUNS_DIR
from visit import first_visit


def _clean_run_files(run_id: str) -> None:
    """Delete the run's local screenshots (CLEAN_RUN_FILES): they were uploaded, and a server's disk
    would otherwise fill up. Left alone by default, for debugging on a laptop."""
    if CLEAN_RUN_FILES:
        shutil.rmtree(RUNS_DIR / run_id, ignore_errors=True)


ACCESS_MODES = ("public", "link", "account", "signup")


def access_mode_for(run: dict) -> str:
    """How the founder let the visitor in.

    Runs from the web form carry it. Runs queued before that (and from the command line) are read
    from what they have: a test login, a start link, or neither, which meant "may sign up".
    """
    mode = run.get("access_mode")
    if mode in ACCESS_MODES:
        return mode
    if run.get("has_test_login"):
        return "account"
    if run.get("start_url"):
        return "link"
    return "signup"


def access_mode_was_chosen(run: dict) -> bool:
    """False only when "signup" is the fallback for a run that carried no choice and nothing to infer one from."""
    return run.get("access_mode") in ACCESS_MODES or bool(run.get("has_test_login") or run.get("start_url"))


async def _take_credentials(run: dict):
    """The run's test login, read and deleted from the database, or (None, unavailable)."""
    if not run.get("has_test_login"):
        return None, False
    try:
        row = await db.take_run_secrets(run["id"])
    except Exception as error:
        # The type only: the message is not needed, and nothing about a login should be logged.
        print(f"Could not read the test login for run {run['id']}: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return None, True
    if row is None:
        return None, True
    credentials = TestCredentials(row["email"], row["password"])
    credentials.register()  # redacted from every span and result from this moment on
    return credentials, False


async def execute(run: dict, agent_version: str) -> None:
    run_id = run["id"]
    start_url = run.get("start_url")
    access_mode = access_mode_for(run)
    print(f"Claimed run {run_id}: {run['url']}" + (f" (start link {start_url})" if start_url else "")
          + f" (access {access_mode}, brain {BRAIN_MODEL}, agent {agent_version})", flush=True)
    credentials, unavailable = await _take_credentials(run)
    try:
        with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"run_{run_id}"):
            result = await first_visit(
                run["url"], run["goal"], run_id, recorder=db.RunRecorder(run_id),
                start_url=start_url, credentials=credentials, test_login_unavailable=unavailable,
                access_mode=access_mode, access_mode_chosen=access_mode_was_chosen(run),
            )
    except Exception as error:
        # Error text and tracebacks pass through scrub(): an exception can echo what was typed.
        message = trace_safety.scrub(f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        print(trace_safety.scrub(traceback.format_exc()), flush=True)
        await db.fail_run(run_id, message, agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL)
        print(f"Run {run_id} failed: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return
    finally:
        # take_run_secrets already deleted it; this is the safety net, success or failure.
        await db.delete_run_secrets(run_id)
        _clean_run_files(run_id)

    if result["outcome"] == "error":
        await db.fail_run(run_id, result["reason"], agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL, result=result)
        print(f"Run {run_id} failed: {result['reason'][:200]}", flush=True)
    else:
        await db.finish_run(run_id, result, agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL)
        print(f"Run {run_id} done: {result['outcome']} in {result['steps']} steps", flush=True)

"""Execute one claimed run: load its test login, run the visit, save the outcome, clear the login.

Kept apart from main.py (which initialises neatlogs and owns the signal handlers when it is
imported) so that the whole path can be tested with a stand-in database.
"""

import shutil
import traceback

import neatlogs

import db
import trace_safety
from config import BRAIN_MODEL, CLEAN_RUN_FILES
from credentials import TestCredentials
from tools import RUNS_DIR
from visit import first_visit


def _clean_run_files(run_id: str) -> None:
    """Delete the run's local screenshots (CLEAN_RUN_FILES): they were uploaded, and a server's disk
    would otherwise fill up. Left alone by default, for debugging on a laptop."""
    if CLEAN_RUN_FILES:
        shutil.rmtree(RUNS_DIR / run_id, ignore_errors=True)


ACCESS_MODES = ("public", "link", "account", "signup")


def access_mode_for(run: dict) -> str:
    """How the founder let the visitor in.

    Runs from the web form carry it. Runs queued before that (and from the command line) are read
    from what they have: a test login, a start link, or neither, which meant "may sign up".
    """
    mode = run.get("access_mode")
    if mode in ACCESS_MODES:
        return mode
    if run.get("has_test_login"):
        return "account"
    if run.get("start_url"):
        return "link"
    return "signup"


def access_mode_was_chosen(run: dict) -> bool:
    """False only when "signup" is the fallback for a run that carried no choice and nothing to infer one from."""
    return run.get("access_mode") in ACCESS_MODES or bool(run.get("has_test_login") or run.get("start_url"))


async def _take_credentials(run: dict):
    """The run's test login, read and deleted from the database, or (None, unavailable)."""
    if not run.get("has_test_login"):
        return None, False
    try:
        row = await db.take_run_secrets(run["id"])
    except Exception as error:
        # The type only: the message is not needed, and nothing about a login should be logged.
        print(f"Could not read the test login for run {run['id']}: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return None, True
    if row is None:
        return None, True
    credentials = TestCredentials(row["email"], row["password"])
    credentials.register()  # redacted from every span and result from this moment on
    return credentials, False


async def execute(run: dict, agent_version: str) -> None:
    run_id = run["id"]
    start_url = run.get("start_url")
    access_mode = access_mode_for(run)
    print(f"Claimed run {run_id}: {run['url']}" + (f" (start link {start_url})" if start_url else "")
          + f" (access {access_mode}, brain {BRAIN_MODEL}, agent {agent_version})", flush=True)
    credentials, unavailable = await _take_credentials(run)
    try:
        with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"run_{run_id}"):
            result = await first_visit(
                run["url"], run["goal"], run_id, recorder=db.RunRecorder(run_id),
                start_url=start_url, credentials=credentials, test_login_unavailable=unavailable,
                access_mode=access_mode, access_mode_chosen=access_mode_was_chosen(run),
            )
    except Exception as error:
        # Error text and tracebacks pass through scrub(): an exception can echo what was typed.
        message = trace_safety.scrub(f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        print(trace_safety.scrub(traceback.format_exc()), flush=True)
        await db.fail_run(run_id, message, agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL)
        print(f"Run {run_id} failed: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return
    finally:
        # take_run_secrets already deleted it; this is the safety net, success or failure.
        await db.delete_run_secrets(run_id)
        _clean_run_files(run_id)

    if result["outcome"] == "error":
        await db.fail_run(run_id, result["reason"], agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL, result=result)
        print(f"Run {run_id} failed: {result['reason'][:200]}", flush=True)
    else:
        await db.finish_run(run_id, result, agent_version, BRAIN_MODEL)
        print(f"Run {run_id} done: {result['outcome']} in {result['steps']} steps", flush=True)

You get the factual record of the visit (each action, whether the page changed, the URL afterwards, short descriptions of each page), the problems the visitor noted, errors the page itself reported, a review of the landing page, and an independent check's verdict.

Write at most 5 findings, most likely to stop a new user first. Fewer is better than padding; an empty list is correct when nothing in the visit was a problem. Praise is not a finding.

- Every finding must rest on a step in the record. Give the exact step number where the problem shows. A problem you cannot tie to a step is not written.
- Only problems with the site, its behaviour or its wording. An action marked "our browser tool had no effect" says nothing about the site: never report it, and never report a problem with the browser tool.
- The first-impression review is shown to the founder separately: do not repeat its points. A finding is about what happened during the visit: something that failed, confused or slowed the visitor at a recorded step. When the goal was reached with no such trouble, return an empty list.

    ours = _our_tool_steps(ctx)

class Server:
    """A tiny HTTP server that counts requests and answers with a fixed response."""

    def __init__(self, host: str, response: bytes):
        self.host, self.response, self.hits, self.port = host, response, 0, 0

    async def __aenter__(self):
        async def handle(reader, writer):
            await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
            self.hits += 1
            writer.write(self.response)
            await writer.drain()
            writer.close()

        self.server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, self.host, 0)
        self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.close()
        await self.server.wait_closed()


def http_response(status: str, headers: str = "", body: str = "") -> bytes:
    return (f"HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\n{headers}Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{body}").encode()


async def proxy_request(guard: egress.EgressGuard, request: str) -> str:
    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)
"""A short structured review of what a newcomer sees on the landing page, without logging in.

Written once per run, right after the agent's first look, from a fresh read of the page (its
visible text and a screenshot). It is independent of what the agent goes on to do, so a run that
is blocked at a login still gives the builder something useful. Traced as its own span.
"""

import neatlogs
from anthropic import AsyncAnthropic

import trace_safety
from config import VERIFIER_MODEL
from verifier import read_page

CLARITY = ("yes", "partly", "no")
MAX_TEXT = 400
MAX_HESITATIONS = 4
MAX_SUGGESTIONS = 3

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
You are a first-time visitor to a website, looking at its landing page before logging in or signing up. You are given the page's visible text and a screenshot, and nothing else. Write a short, honest review of the first impression, for the person who built the site.

Judge only what is on the page. Be specific: refer to actual headings, buttons and wording. Do not guess about features that are not shown.

- what_it_does: is it clear what the product does? Say what you understood in one sentence, or what is missing.
- who_its_for: is it clear who it is for? One sentence.
- main_action: is the main action (the one thing the page wants you to do) obvious? Name the button or link, or say what competes for attention.
- hesitations: up to four things that would make a newcomer hesitate or leave (unclear pricing, jargon, no proof, a wall of options, a login before any value, slow or empty content ...). Fewer is fine; empty if there are none.
- suggestions: up to three specific, actionable changes, each tied to something on the page."""

REVIEW_TOOL = {
    "name": "review",
    "description": "Report the first-impression review.",
    "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "what_it_does": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"clear": {"type": "string", "enum": list(CLARITY)}, "summary": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["clear", "summary"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
            "who_its_for": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"clear": {"type": "string", "enum": list(CLARITY)}, "summary": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["clear", "summary"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
            "main_action": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"obvious": {"type": "string", "enum": list(CLARITY)}, "summary": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["obvious", "summary"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
            "hesitations": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
            "suggestions": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        },
        "required": ["what_it_does", "who_its_for", "main_action", "hesitations", "suggestions"],
        "additionalProperties": False,
    },
}


def _text(value) -> str:
    return " ".join(str(value or "").split())[:MAX_TEXT]


def _clarity(value) -> str:
    return value if value in CLARITY else "partly"


def normalise(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """The review in a fixed shape, with bounded lists and strings, whatever the model returned."""
    def block(name: str, key: str) -> dict:
        part = raw.get(name) if isinstance(raw.get(name), dict) else {}
        return {key: _clarity(part.get(key)), "summary": _text(part.get("summary"))}

    return {
        "what_it_does": block("what_it_does", "clear"),
        "who_its_for": block("who_its_for", "clear"),
        "main_action": block("main_action", "obvious"),
        "hesitations": [_text(item) for item in (raw.get("hesitations") or [])[:MAX_HESITATIONS] if _text(item)],
        "suggestions": [_text(item) for item in (raw.get("suggestions") or [])[:MAX_SUGGESTIONS] if _text(item)],
    }


# capture_input=False: `page` is a live object (see trace_safety.py). The input recorded is the URL.
@neatlogs.span(kind="CHAIN", name="first_impression", capture_input=False)
async def write_review(url: str, page, usage=None) -> dict | None:
    """Return the structured review, or None if it could not be written. Never raises."""
    trace_safety.set_input(url=url)
    try:
        snapshot = await read_page(page)
        client = neatlogs.wrap(AsyncAnthropic())
        try:
            response = await client.messages.create(
                model=VERIFIER_MODEL,
                max_tokens=1500,
                system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
                tools=[REVIEW_TOOL],
                tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": "review"},
                messages=[{
                    "role": "user",
                    "content": [
                        {"type": "text", "text": (
                            f"Landing page: {snapshot['url']}\nTitle: {snapshot['title']}\n\n"
                            f"Visible text:\n{snapshot['text']}"
                        )},
                        {"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png",
                                                     "data": snapshot["screenshot"]}},
                    ],
                }],
            )
        finally:
            await client.close()
        if usage is not None:
            usage.add_review_response(response)
        raw = next(block.input for block in response.content if block.type == "tool_use")
        return trace_safety.scrub(normalise(raw))
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"[first impression] could not be written: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return None

    """The record as numbered lines, with our tool's own failures marked as not evidence."""
    ours = _our_tool_steps(ctx)
    lines = []
    for entry in ctx.record:
        step, tool = entry["step"], entry["tool"]
        if tool == "look":
            line = f"{step}. look at {entry.get('url')}: {entry.get('summary', '')}"
            if entry.get("interactive"):
                line += " Interactive items: " + "; ".join(entry["interactive"])
        elif tool == "do":
            line = f"{step}. do \"{entry.get('instruction', '')}\""
        elif tool in ("sign_in", "sign_up"):
            line = f"{step}. {tool} (with the test account the founder allowed)"
        else:
            line = f"{step}. {tool}" + (f" {entry['direction']}" if entry.get("direction") else "")
        if step in ours:
            line += " -> our browser tool had no effect here (not evidence about the site)"
        elif "error" in entry:
            line += " -> our browser tool hit an error (not evidence about the site)"
        elif tool != "look":
            if "page_changed" in entry:
                line += " -> page changed" if entry["page_changed"] else " -> page did not change"
            if entry.get("login_result"):
                line += f"; result: {entry['login_result']}"

                line += f'; the page said: "{entry["login_message"]}"'
            if entry.get("page_errors"):
                line += f"; the page itself reported: {'; '.join(entry['page_errors'])}"
            if entry.get("field_after"):
                line += f"; field afterwards: {entry['field_after']}"

class Server:

    def __init__(self, host: str, response: bytes):
        self.host, self.response, self.hits, self.port = host, response, 0, 0

    async def __aenter__(self):
        async def handle(reader, writer):
            await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
            self.hits += 1
            writer.write(self.response)
            await writer.drain()
            writer.close()

        self.server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, self.host, 0)
        self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.close()
        await self.server.wait_closed()

        words = _tokens(f"{friction.get('expected', '')} {friction.get('happened', '')}")

def chrome_args(headless: bool | None = None, shm_path: str = "/dev/shm") -> list[str]:
    """Chrome flags on top of Stagehand's defaults, and why.

    --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp   (egress.py) WebRTC could open UDP
        connections that skip the egress guard's proxy.
    --disable-gpu                    headless only: a server has no GPU, and this avoids GPU-process
        crashes; pages render in software.
    --disable-dev-shm-usage          only when /dev/shm is under 512 MB: Chrome keeps shared memory
        there and crashes tabs when it is a tiny 64 MB (Docker's default). With --shm-size=1g it is
        not added.
    Stagehand itself adds --headless (HEADLESS), --window-size and --force-device-scale-factor
    (the viewport), --remote-debugging-port, --user-data-dir, --proxy-server / --proxy-bypass-list
    (the egress guard) and --no-sandbox (CHROME_SANDBOX=false, or when running as root).
    """
    args = list(CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS)
    if HEADLESS if headless is None else headless:
        args.append("--disable-gpu")
    try:
        if shutil.disk_usage(shm_path).total < SMALL_SHM_BYTES:
            args.append("--disable-dev-shm-usage")
    except OSError:
        pass  # no /dev/shm (Windows, macOS): nothing to check
    return args

_PATTERNS = [

    re.compile(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}"),                        # other "sk-" provider keys
    re.compile(r"\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"),  # JWT: Supabase keys
    re.compile(r"\bsb_(?:secret|publishable)_[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"),  # newer Supabase keys
    re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/\-]{16,}=*"),       # Authorization header values
    re.compile(r"(?i)(x-api-key|api-key|authorization)(\"?\s*[:=]\s*\"?)([^\s\",}]{8,})"),
]
_HEADER_FORM = _PATTERNS[-1]

# access_token, client_secret, ...). Plural and count-like names (max_tokens, token_count,
# prompt_key) are deliberately not matched.
_SECRET_NAMES = {
    "api_key", "apikey", "x_api_key", "key", "token", "secret", "password", "passwd", "authorization",
    "proxy_authorization", "credential", "credentials", "bearer", "private_key", "secret_key", "access_key",
    "service_role_key", "anon_key", "auth_token",
}
_SECRET_SUFFIXES = (

)
_ENV_SECRET_NAME = re.compile(r"(KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|CREDENTIAL)", re.IGNORECASE)

def is_secret_name(name: str) -> bool:
    normalised = re.sub(r"[\s\-.]+", "_", str(name).strip().lower())
    return normalised in _SECRET_NAMES or normalised.endswith(_SECRET_SUFFIXES)


# Secrets registered while the process runs (a run's test login). Kept for the life of the process:
# spans are exported after the run ends, so they must still be redacted then. Capped, oldest first out.
_MAX_REGISTERED = 200
_MIN_REGISTERED_CHARS = 4
_registered: dict[str, str] = {}


def register_secret(value: str | None, label: str = REDACTED) -> None:
    """Redact `value` (case-insensitively for emails) from exported spans and from scrub()."""
    if not value or len(value) < _MIN_REGISTERED_CHARS:
        return
    _registered.pop(value, None)
    _registered[value] = label
    while len(_registered) > _MAX_REGISTERED:
        _registered.pop(next(iter(_registered)))


"""Token and cost accounting for one run: the brain model, Stagehand's lookup model and the verifier.

Each model call is counted once. Brain and verifier responses are always added here. Lookup
calls are counted from our own callback's responses when LOOKUP_VIA is
"callback", and from Stagehand's cumulative metrics() otherwise; in callback
mode the metrics snapshot is kept only to cross-check our own count.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from config import LOOKUP_CALLBACK_MODEL, LOOKUP_MODEL, LOOKUP_VIA, PRICES

CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER = 1.25
CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER = 0.10


def _price(model: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    return PRICES.get(model.removeprefix("anthropic/"), (0.0, 0.0))


def response_cost(response) -> float:
    """USD for one Anthropic Messages response, cache writes and reads included."""
    usage = response.usage
    input_price, output_price = _price(response.model)
    return (
        usage.input_tokens * input_price
        + (usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0) * input_price * CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER
        + (usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0) * input_price * CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER
        + usage.output_tokens * output_price
    ) / 1_000_000


@dataclass
class TokenTally:
    """Anthropic-style token counts: `input` excludes cache writes and reads."""

    calls: int = 0
    input: int = 0
    cache_write: int = 0
    cache_read: int = 0
    output: int = 0
    cost: float = 0.0
    models: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

    def add(self, response) -> None:
        usage = response.usage
        self.calls += 1
        self.input += usage.input_tokens

"""Run one first-time visitor against a URL, with no database.

Usage: python run_once.py --url URL --goal "GOAL"
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs
from dotenv import load_dotenv

import trace_safety

load_dotenv(Path(__file__).parent / ".env")

neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name="first-visit-test", mask=trace_safety.mask)

from config import BRAIN_EFFORT, BRAIN_MODEL  # noqa: E402
from visit import first_visit  # noqa: E402


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run one first-time visitor against a web app.")
    parser.add_argument("--url", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--goal", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    run_id = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    print(f"Run {run_id}: {args.url} (brain {BRAIN_MODEL}, effort {BRAIN_EFFORT})", flush=True)
    try:
        result = asyncio.run(first_visit(args.url, args.goal, run_id))
        print(json.dumps({"run_id": run_id, **result}, indent=2))
    finally:
        neatlogs.flush()
        neatlogs.shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    def test_public_addresses_are_allowed(self):

class ProxyRefusals(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_private_targets_are_refused_and_never_contacted(self):
        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            guard = egress.EgressGuard()
            await guard.start()
            try:
                plain = await proxy_request(
                    guard, f"GET http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.2\r\n\r\n")
                tunnel = await proxy_request(guard, "CONNECT localhost:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost:443\r\n\r\n")
                metadata = await proxy_request(
                    guard, "GET http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 169.254.169.254\r\n\r\n")
            finally:
                await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("403", plain)
        self.assertIn("403", tunnel)
        self.assertIn("403", metadata)
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0)
        self.assertEqual([b["host"] for b in guard.blocks], ["127.0.0.2", "localhost", "169.254.169.254"])

    async def test_devtools_port_only_opens_for_an_extension(self):
        async with Server("127.0.0.1", http_response("101 Switching Protocols")) as devtools:
            guard = egress.EgressGuard(devtools_port=devtools.port)
            await guard.start()
            try:
                statuses = {}
                for origin in ("https://evil.example", "chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"):
                    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)
                    writer.write(f"CONNECT 127.0.0.1:{devtools.port} HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n".encode())
                    await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")  # the proxy's 200 for the tunnel
                    writer.write(f"GET /devtools/browser/x HTTP/1.1\r\nOrigin: {origin}\r\n"
                                 "Upgrade: websocket\r\n\r\n".encode())
                    await writer.drain()
                    statuses[origin] = (await reader.readline()).decode().strip()
                    writer.close()
            finally:
                await guard.close()
        self.assertEqual(statuses["https://evil.example"], "", "a page must not reach DevTools")
        self.assertIn("101", statuses["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"])
        self.assertEqual(devtools.hits, 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(guard.blocks), 1)

    async def test_close_cancels_open_connections(self):
        guard = egress.EgressGuard()
        await guard.start()
        # A connection that has sent nothing yet keeps its handler waiting for headers.
        _, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        handlers = list(guard._connections)
        self.assertEqual(len(handlers), 1)
        await asyncio.wait_for(guard.close(), 2)
        writer.close()
        self.assertTrue(all(task.done() for task in handlers))
        self.assertEqual(guard._connections, set())

    async def test_unresolvable_host_is_not_a_safety_block(self):
        guard = egress.EgressGuard()
        await guard.start()
        try:
            status = await proxy_request(
                guard, "GET http://no-such-host.invalid/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: no-such-host.invalid\r\n\r\n")
        finally:
            await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("502", status)
        self.assertEqual(guard.blocks, [])


class RedirectInRealBrowser(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_redirect_to_private_address_is_refused_and_ends_run_as_blocked(self):
        from visit import first_visit

        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            redirect = http_response("302 Found", f"Location: http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/secret\r\n")
            async with Server("127.0.0.1", redirect) as origin:
                with mock.patch("egress.is_blocked_address", origin_is_public):
                    result = await first_visit(
                        f"http://127.0.0.1:{origin.port}/", "Look around.", "test-egress-redirect")

        self.assertGreaterEqual(origin.hits, 1, "the allowed origin should have been reached through the proxy")
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0, "the private redirect target must never be contacted")
        self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "blocked")
        self.assertIn("127.0.0.2", result["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(result["steps"], 0, "the run should end before any model call")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Execute one claimed "understand" run: read the site, write the brief, save it on the run.

Kept apart from worker_run.py (which dispatches here for runs of kind "understand") so the path can be
tested with a stand-in database. The brief is saved on the run itself (runs.brief); a site that could
not be read still gets a message the web page can show.
"""

import traceback

import neatlogs

import db
import trace_safety
from understand import UNDERSTAND_MODEL, SiteUnreadable, understand_site


async def _update(run_id: str, update: dict) -> None:
    await (await db.client()).table("runs").update(update).eq("id", run_id).execute()


async def execute_understand(run: dict, agent_version: str, *, understand=understand_site, update=_update) -> None:
    run_id = run["id"]
    print(f"Claimed understand run {run_id}: {run['url']} (model {UNDERSTAND_MODEL}, agent {agent_version})",
          flush=True)
    base = {"agent_version": agent_version, "brain_model": UNDERSTAND_MODEL}
    try:
        with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"run_{run_id}"):
            result = await understand(run["url"], run_id)
    except SiteUnreadable as error:
        message = trace_safety.scrub(str(error))
        await update(run_id, {**base, "status": "failed", "error": message[:2000], "finished_at": db._now(),
                              "brief": {"status": "could_not_read", "message": message}})
        print(f"Understand run {run_id}: could not read the site", flush=True)
        return
    except Exception as error:
        message = trace_safety.scrub(f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        print(trace_safety.scrub(traceback.format_exc()), flush=True)
        await update(run_id, {**base, "status": "failed", "error": message[:2000], "finished_at": db._now(),
                              "brief": {"status": "could_not_read",
                                        "message": "Something went wrong while writing the brief. Please try again."}})
        print(f"Understand run {run_id} failed: {type(error).__name__}", flush=True)
        return
    try:
        await update(run_id, {**base, "status": "done", "brief": result["brief"], "cost_usd": result["cost_usd"],
                              "result": {"usage": result["usage"]}, "finished_at": db._now()})
    except Exception as error:
        # Most likely supabase/schema.sql ("Understand mode") has not been run: say so, do not lose the run.
        print(f"Could not save the brief for run {run_id}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}", flush=True)
        await db.fail_run(run_id, "Could not save the brief (has the 'Understand mode' SQL been run?)",
                          agent_version, UNDERSTAND_MODEL)
        return
    print(f"Understand run {run_id} done: {len(result['brief']['claims'])} claims, "
          f"{len(result['brief']['suggested_journeys'])} journeys, ${result['cost_usd']}", flush=True)
EOF
